problemStatement.formal: f_3(n)=\max\{|S|:S\subseteq\{0,1,2\}^n,\ S\text{ contains no three-term combinatorial line}\},\quad f_3(n)=o(3^n).
problemStatement.plain: Formalize Erdos problem 185 on cap sets in the ternary hypercube. The Lean file defines cap sets, proves elementary finite cases and lower-bound constructions, and derives the asymptotic answer from an axiomatized density Hales-Jewett input.
whyMatters: Cap sets are a central bridge between extremal combinatorics, additive combinatorics, and polynomial-method ideas.
The ternary hypercube model gives concrete finite examples such as `f3 1`, `f3 2`, `f3 3`, and `f3 4`.
The final asymptotic answer is mathematically known, but this Lean entry still depends on external theorem axioms.

proven: `IsCapSet` defines cap sets in `{0,1,2}^n`, and `isCapSet_empty`/`isCapSet_singleton` prove base examples.
`f3_1`, `f3_2`, `f3_3`, and `f3_4` compute the first nontrivial maximum cap-set sizes.
`binaryCubeImg_isCapSet` and `f3_ge_two_pow` give a uniform binary-cube lower bound.
`erdos_185`, `erdos_185_density`, and `erdos_185_answer` derive the little-o answer from the axiomatized density Hales-Jewett theorem.
open: `density_hales_jewett_k3` and `meshulam_upper_bound` are axioms, so the global asymptotic result is imported rather than proved internally.
knownResults.goal: Record the completed cap-set metadata with a clear split between proved finite/combinatorial infrastructure and axiom-backed asymptotic theory.
